subject: pathology
title: Haematopoietic Stem Cells, Marrow Examination, and Aplastic Anaemia

steps.tx: Every blood cell descends from haematopoietic stem cells that self renew and differentiate through committed progenitors under cytokine instruction, residing in marrow niches and marked by CD34. Transplantation exploits their ability to rebuild an entire blood system from a small inoculum; the founding cell is the **haematopoietic stem cell**.
steps.say: One stem cell population rebuilds the entire blood; CD34 marks it and transplantation proves it.

nodes.label: Stem cell self renews in marrow niche
Cytokines steer red, white, platelet output
Mature cells enter blood for finite lifespans

steps.tx: Erythropoiesis answers renal oxygen sensing: falling oxygen raises erythropoietin, marrow releases reticulocytes within days, and the reticulocyte count therefore reports real time red cell production in any anaemia. A low count in severe anaemia convicts the marrow; the production gauge is the **reticulocyte count**.
steps.say: The reticulocyte count is the marrow's live production report; inappropriately low values convict production failure.

steps.tx: Bone marrow aspiration smears cytology of individual cells while trephine biopsy preserves architecture, cellularity, fibrosis, and infiltrates, so the two procedures answer different questions and are usually performed together. Fat replacing marrow with age recalibrates what cellularity is normal; the architecture specimen is the **trephine biopsy**.
steps.say: Aspiration shows the cells, trephine shows the city plan; do both when the marrow itself is the question.

left.title: Marrow aspiration
points: Dry tap when fibrotic or packed

steps.tx: Place the two trephine cores next to each other. The first is packed with developing blood cells of every lineage, while the second is mostly empty fat spaces with barely a haematopoietic cell in sight. That fatty, deserted core is the biopsy face of **aplastic marrow**, explaining pancytopenia far better than any single blood count value can.
steps.say: Side by side, one trephine core is full of blood forming cells and the other is mostly fat. That empty fatty core is aplastic marrow, and it explains the pancytopenia.

vis.alt: Bone marrow trephine biopsy showing normal cellular marrow beside fatty aplastic marrow with almost no haematopoietic cells
vis.caption: Bone marrow trephine biopsy showing normal cellular marrow beside fatty aplastic marrow with almost no haematopoietic cells. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Aplastic anaemia empties the marrow through immune T cell attack on stem cells, leaving pancytopenia with a fatty hypocellular trephine and no blasts, splenomegaly, or dysplasia. Drugs, hepatitis, and inherited syndromes trigger some cases; the defining lesion is **immune marrow failure**.
steps.say: Aplastic anaemia is an empty fatty marrow with pancytopenia, most often an immune attack on stem cells.

vis.caption: Aplastic anaemia overview showing hypocellular marrow and pancytopenia.

steps.tx: Fanconi anaemia inherits broken DNA crosslink repair, presenting with short stature, thumb and radial anomalies, skin pigmentation, and childhood marrow failure with high cancer risk. Chromosomal breakage testing with diepoxybutane confirms the diagnosis of **Fanconi anaemia** before transplant planning. Mitomycin C serves as the alternative breakage agent in laboratories without diepoxybutane access.
steps.say: Thumb anomalies, short stature, and childhood marrow failure mean Fanconi anaemia; test chromosomal breakage before transplant.

left.title: Acquired aplastic anaemia
points: Immune stem cell attack, any age

steps.tx: Fanconi anaemia is inherited failure of DNA crosslink repair. Children are short, thumbs and radii are anomalous, skin is pigmented, marrow fails early, and cancer risk is high. Diepoxybutane chromosomal breakage testing confirms **Fanconi anaemia** before transplant is planned, and mitomycin C is the substitute agent if diepoxybutane is unavailable. Myelophthisic anaemia empties the marrow another way: fibrosis or tumour crowds out normal cells, and the film shows teardrop red cells plus a leucoerythroblastic picture of immature white and red cells spilled early.
steps.say: Short stature, abnormal thumbs and radii, pigmented skin, and childhood marrow failure suggest Fanconi anaemia, confirmed by chromosomal breakage with diepoxybutane or mitomycin C before transplant. Myelophthisic anaemia instead fills the marrow with fibrosis or tumour. Teardrop red cells and early white and red cell precursors on the film show that replacement.

vis.alt: Marrow crowded by fibrosis and tumour, with teardrop red cells and immature white and red cells on the blood film.
vis.caption: Normal marrow is replaced by fibrosis and tumour, and the film shows teardrop cells plus early white and red cell precursors. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: A marrow crowded out by tumour or fibrosis fails with a distinctive blood film. **Myelophthisic anaemia** shows teardrop red cells and early white and platelet precursors escaping together, the leukoerythroblastic picture of a marrow whose architecture is destroyed. The smear redirects the search from iron and vitamins to imaging and biopsy of the marrow space itself. In children and adults alike, that film pattern is a structural diagnosis asking for its cause.
steps.say: Myelophthisic anaemia gives teardrop cells and early precursors on film from a marrow replaced by tumour or fibrosis. The film demands a marrow search.

vis.alt: Blood film image of myelophthisic anaemia with teardrop cells and immature precursors.
vis.caption: Teardrop red cells and early white precursors crowd a leukoerythroblastic blood film. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Pure red cell aplasia isolates the failure to one lineage: Diamond-Blackfan anaemia presents in infancy with ribosomal protein mutations and congenital anomalies, while acquired disease follows thymoma, parvovirus B19, or drugs. Transfusion dependence with absent erythroid precursors defines **pure red cell aplasia**.
steps.say: When only red cells fail, think Diamond-Blackfan in infants and parvovirus B19 or thymoma in adults.

steps.tx: Myelophthisic anaemia results when fibrosis, metastatic cancer, or granulomas physically replace marrow, releasing nucleated red cells and early white precursors into blood with teardrop poikilocytes. The leucoerythroblastic film is a biopsy summons; the process is **myelophthisic anaemia**. Primary myelofibrosis is the classic marrow native cause behind this alarming blood film pattern.
steps.say: Teardrop cells with nucleated red cells in blood mean the marrow is being replaced; biopsy will show by what.

vis.caption: Systemic iron homeostasis and transport, the supply chain erythropoiesis depends upon.

steps.tx: Treatment of severe aplastic anaemia chooses between matched sibling transplantation for the young and immunosuppression with antithymocyte globulin, ciclosporin, and eltrombopag for others, while transfusion support is given cautiously to protect transplant options. Early specialist referral decides outcomes; the strategy is **marrow failure triage** by severity and donor.
steps.say: Young patients with a matched sibling go to transplant; others receive immunosuppression plus eltrombopag, referred early.
